properties.name: The Flats
properties.notes: Occupancy 88.39% (93.75% leased); 4 units rent-ready. Collections slipped to 87.5% with ~$10,684 in 0-30 day delinquency, over $9,800 of it across five tenants. Approved $10-$49 rent reductions on select units; classic studio rates held. November renewals only 40%. Maintenance destabilized by Chad's resignation - Gary covering interim at $40/hr vs ~$33 budget; $500 signing bonus over 90 days proposed and an internal promotion is being pursued. Work orders cut from 30 to 13. Apartments.com cancelled effective Sept 30; zero Zillow applications or leases and a weak 22.6% tour-to-application rate.

properties.name: Nightingale on 25th
properties.notes: Remains under full passive lender operational control with no foreclosure filing and no clear exit plan. Occupancy approximately 80%. Interest-rate conditions remain unfavorable for any refinancing or exit. Flagged in the 2026 audit as a likely write-down to zero valuation. No ZMR-run weekly operations call this week - status derived from the Atlantic Creek monthly call and the Baker Tilly audit planning session. Nightingale Q2 data is being used to validate the new Q3 reporting automation prototype.

properties.name: The Julia
properties.notes: Occupancy stable at 90.31%, projected 90.62% after scheduled move-ins; four move-ins against five move-outs last week. Seven tours produced five applications. November renewals sluggish, so the renewal incentive was raised from $350 to $500 with the 20th-of-month deadline held. Three tenants received visa denials - one departure already, another surrender expected; no ICE raids reported. Delinquency approximately $26,000 across 15 tenants with only ~$4,000 aged past 31 days. Maintenance staffing constrained after two failed interviews; one candidate in training plus a possible internal transfer. Open work orders declining into the 60s. Reservation of Rights document awaiting a funding-assurance clarification before signature.

properties.name: The Boardwalk
properties.notes: Occupancy 85%. Month-to-date collections approximately 89.4% with delinquency near $50,158. Leasing constrained by unit readiness - five units leased last week against a 29-unit month-end goal; team exploring vendor support to lift turns from five to seven-to-ten per week. Renewal campaign launches 09/21 with a three-month concession. Vendors being used to accelerate complex work. Digital marketing improving: leads up to 57 and leases to 10, prompting a 20% PPC increase and an Apartments.com downgrade to Gold by Nov 1. Newmark lender-required repairs (curbing, asphalt patching, landscaping, ~$18,500 budget) remain in dispute - lender re-inspection still flags items and invoices, payment proof and before/after photos are outstanding.

properties.name: Hanley Place
properties.notes: Strongest occupancy in the Florida portfolio at 95%, and cited in the 2026 audit as one of only two clearly performing assets. The problem is the balance sheet: over $700,000 in aging payables with the cause not yet diagnosed - Jimmy Chestnut is reviewing the AP ballooning alongside the outstanding roofer report. Service manager position needs backfilling. Newmark lender repairs largely completed in-house (ADA curb work, Ring camera, landscaping, painting, down-unit repairs) against a ~$10,000 landscaping budget, but supporting documentation is missing and soffit repairs at Buildings 28 and 36 remain unverified.

properties.name: Skye at Conway
properties.notes: Best-in-class week. Occupancy reached 93% with pre-leasing at 95.91% and a 50% close rate (three leases from six tours). Delinquency minimal - a single pending payment - and the property ranks near the top of the portfolio on collections. Application fees rising to $50 and admin to $99 to filter out speculative applications; two-bedroom units will be held 30 days post-signing pending utility transfer. $500 renewal incentive for leases signed by Sept 30 and a $500 resident referral program both running. Dog park and basketball court security upgrades land by end of next week; gutter drainage repairs rescheduled to Saturday. A $117,000 waterfall release will fund prioritized vendor payments - HD Supply is locked pending payment, with Chadwell as backup. Lender site visit Thursday.

properties.name: Skye Oaks (Palms at Palisades)
properties.notes: Reported operationally as part of the combined Sky Oaks campus - occupancy approximately 91% with a 3% improvement in collections. Newmark lender repair work is the binding constraint ahead of the Sept 30 deadline: unit electrical complete, GFCI outlets and panel replacements roughly 90% done and in final inspection, car-wash station electrical complete but awaiting county permit sign-off. Curb repairs at two of three buildings (638 and 642) remain outstanding and extensive asphalt cracking needs lender guidance because the ~$22,500 budget supports patching rather than remilling. Property inspections are complete. Marketing turned sharply positive - leases quadrupled and cost per lease nearly halved after a website refresh and higher PMAX spend - though tour attendance and tour-to-lease conversion remain weak.

properties.name: Skye Oaks (Brandon Oaks)
properties.notes: Reported operationally as part of the combined Sky Oaks campus - occupancy approximately 91% with a 3% improvement in collections. Same Newmark lender repair exposure as the Palisades parcel with a hard Sept 30 deadline: GFCI and panel work in final inspection, county permit sign-off pending on car-wash electrical, curb repairs outstanding at Buildings 638 and 642, and asphalt scope unresolved against a ~$22,500 budget. Garrett is pulling Yardi payment records and Sidonio is on site collecting photographic evidence. Zillow package being reduced to mid-tier with $300/month SEO spend resuming.

properties.name: Skye Reserve
properties.notes: The portfolio's largest and most troubled asset. Occupancy approximately 78% (76.37% at the low) against a projection of 79.1-79.2%; pending applications cleaned up from 79 to 34. Collections 87% as of the 13th with seven evictions tracked. Thirty-one units are down or admin-classified and require a formal remediation plan with cost detail - Garrett needs a clean, consistently-worded report for the lender. Vendor payables approach $800,000; a $144,000 draw request is being prepared against aging AP. Staffing is the root cause: Brian cannot relocate to Tampa, Tina's role needs backfilling, and Ed is being pulled in at ~25% for three to four months while Julie's portfolio is lightened to add on-site time. Jeremy is now on site daily and lease execution has accelerated. Separately, MF1/Berkshire negotiations converged on a $10 million equity injection, but the interest reserve is far apart ($4 million versus $850,000); debt yield moved to 2.5%, waterfall settled at 1.5%, CBRE BOV approximately $130 million, term sheet expected this week. Marketing is the bright spot - leases rose from 21 to 45 with cost per lease down over $100.

properties.name: Preserve at Riverwalk
properties.notes: Valuation and funding stress. A comparable sale implies approximately $80.55 million against a $98 million acquisition price, with a $66.4 million loan balance outstanding - equity is deeply impaired. Roughly $7-8 million has been contributed since acquisition and the property is approaching capital call 19 or 20; Q2 additional contributions were $1.299 million against $46.897 million of equity invested to date. Capital reconciliation still carries a $50,000 variance with an unexplained additional paid-in-capital entry, and a June contribution was misposted to July in Yardi. Draw mechanics are worsening: approximately $130,000 in reallocations targeted for Draw 19 (Draw 18 was ~$173,000), and every capital draw on the Preserve loan now requires a title search plus a $175 wire. No operations metrics were reported this week.

properties.name: Skye at Hunter's Creek
properties.notes: Meaningfully improving. Occupancy 90.74% with 30- and 60-day projections at 95.3% and an overall trend of 94.4%. Nine tours produced eight applications at a 75% closing ratio; turnover just 4.63% and delinquency exceptionally low. A flash sale (one month free on 1BR/2BR, two months on 3BR) pulled leasing forward ahead of the seasonal slowdown, and the team now plans to taper concessions and raise application and admin fees as availability tightens. October renewals 67% closed. Signature upgrade cost dropped to $1,950 per unit from $2,500. Fire-life-safety work sequenced: painted sprinkler-head corrections in September, breezeway lighting by Oct 10, smoke detector replacement mid-to-late October. Two watch items: the property missed the lender's debt yield test by roughly $20,000 and is targeting a year-end exit from cash management, and cash is short while Silver Cap holds funds - the team is seeking release of $120,000-$160,000 to cover accounts payable. Google rating 4.4.

properties.name: Park at Peachtree Hills
properties.notes: Highest occupancy in the portfolio at 97.5%, up from 96.6% on a Monday move-in, with five tours completed and three more scheduled. Application and admin fees waived as a closing incentive for October and November leases; the $1,450 rental rate held. Preferred-employer program being revived at roughly $525-$550 of value (waived fees plus $275 off first month) with an industry-targeted website tab. Collections 91.3% of total charges and 93% of rental income, approximately $7,000 uncollected; seven-day abandonment notices posted on units C8, C9 and J4. Unit J4 slated for partial renovation - appliances, flooring, kitchen and bath resurfacing - under $5,000 targeting $1,325 rent. Four October renewals signed with a reduced 1.2% increase on B8. Resident referral special raised to $750 for 30 days. Tree permits, paver replacement, bollard removal, downspout and gutter work all in bid.

properties.name: Upland Townhomes
properties.notes: Occupancy healthy at 92.24% with 96% pre-leased, ten tours, five applications and 14 pending; five move-ins against four move-outs expected in 30 days. Rates held with no new concessions. Collections are the issue - improved from 72% to 80% but far below the ~97% target, which drops effective occupancy to roughly 72%. Outstanding balances total $114,000 among residents moved in over two months, including ~$40,000 tied to about 40 recent residents and nearly $50,000 in concessions running longer than eight weeks; over $57,000 is expected by month-end. Screening is tightening materially: second-chance approvals ended, applicants with prior evictions or bankruptcies denied, TransUnion eviction-risk scores layered into the delinquency report alongside move-in dates and 12-month late-payment history. Residents with four or more late payments and 61-day balances are candidates for non-renewal. Business license inspection covering 87 units plus all exteriors; plumbing is the top capital priority; draft budget due the 18th.

properties.name: Ninety-Nine 44
properties.notes: Leasing activity slower than sister property Parks at Walnut, which is undercutting it on rent in the same submarket. Response is a targeted rent reduction plus $500 concessions to restore demand, along with a correction to mispriced loss-leader listings on A3P floor plans. Renewal outreach is being pushed on non-responsive residents. A digital marketing audit is underway for 9944 to refine targeting, messaging and lead qualification. No discrete occupancy or collections figure was reported this week - the asset is covered inside the combined Walnut portfolio call.

properties.name: Parks At Walnut
properties.notes: Strong leasing week - 17 applications, seven approvals, frequent move-ins and 11 vacant rent-ready units. Collections addressing approximately $26,000 owed with $2,000 incoming against a 94-96% target; eviction filings scheduled for Sept 18. Fully staffed. Capital work progressing: signage, pool deck and tree trimming complete, asphalt work begins Sept 21, though landscaping bids came in above the $5,400 budget and vendors have been asked to rebid. An $8,000 vendor payment was delayed and balcony plus asphalt costs are coming. Marketing momentum is good - Google score up to 4.1, $750 referral incentive, resident events - and the property has the best cost per conversion in the Central/West group at $31.22, earning a recommended $500/month PMAX increase funded by the Apartments.com cancellation. Site visit Thursday 9:00-11:30 AM.

properties.name: Chimney Hill
properties.notes: Occupancy is holding at 92% but the credit quality underneath it is deteriorating badly - bad debt reached nearly 19.7% by the 16th, the worst reading in the portfolio, against rent collection of 92.7% versus a 95% target. Delinquency reporting is also unreliable, with discrepancies up to $30,000 caused by past-due notices being incorrectly included. Approximately $6,000 in rental assistance was received and roughly $24,000 of the $30,000 in the 0-30 day bucket is expected to be collected, excluding residents already in eviction. Three-business-day notice requirements plus weekends and holidays are delaying filings. The team is standardizing delinquency reports, adding eviction history, and building a payment-pattern column to drive non-renewal decisions on chronic late payers. Marketing is also underperforming - lead-to-prospect conversion fell 30%, triggering a digital audit, though PPC cost per conversion is a healthy ~$46 against a $150 benchmark. Preferred-employer program relaunching with a Rent Cafe landing page.

properties.name: Skye Isle
properties.notes: Operationally the stronger of the two Dallas Skye assets - occupancy 93.18% with a four-week projection of 95.13% and fast unit turnover. Marketing is productive at 204 leads and 18 leases. The risk here is municipal and legal, not operational: the city is moving toward a habitual crime property designation, with outside counsel coordinating all communications and preparing for the city hearing - all city or external requests must route through the attorney. Related litigation support is being slowed by delays in obtaining police reports and records, which is accruing penalties; a lawsuit against the city was weighed but judged costly, lengthy and uncertain, so negotiating the penalty amount is the preferred path. Separately, the floodplain encampment issue near the creek remains unresolved - the city arborist must confirm whether creek-side trees are protected before any removal, and floodplain rules limit fencing to water-permeable structures that cannot fully span the creek. Coordination with adjacent cemetery security is being explored. Renewals pending; make-ready painting and resurfacing underway.

properties.name: Skye at Love
properties.notes: Crossed the 90% occupancy mark during the week and sits at 89.77% against a 95% budget, projected to 90.91% on 19 move-ins versus 12 move-outs. Leasing demand is strong; the bottleneck is make-ready throughput with 21 vacant not-ready units. Joshua Austin recommended outsourcing ten units to an external vendor at $250-$300 per unit. Renewals are the second problem - September renewal rate 76.19% - with time-limited offers, targeted rent increases, door-to-door resident outreach and pizza incentives proposed as the response. One eviction writ pending. Property is fully staffed. Water billing under audit review with the Urs firm, alarm system installation awaiting a vendor start date, and fire extinguisher inspection out to bid. Waterfall draws due to the lender by end of day. Refinancing discussions continue alongside Skye Ridge.

properties.name: Skye Ridge
properties.notes: Lease rate 94.44% and trending toward 94% occupancy with 14 vacant units, but the renewal pipeline is the alarm: October retention 53.33% on three new renewals and November retention just 9% because of evictions and prior move-outs. Eleven total vacates including eight notices and three pending court actions. Collections 88.1% and down 4% period-over-period, with an early-payment raffle, door knocking, calls and emails deployed in response. Referral fee increase from $500 to $1,000 proposed against a competitor paying $1,200 - pending Nicole's approval. Courtesy patrol costs could rise from $1,800 to $2,670; the team deferred additional patrols absent further incidents and is running resident security education plus a Sept 29 event. Six parking spaces remain out of service on carport damage with repairs held pending budget. A roughly $300,000 capital request is being prepared to clear shortfalls. Apartments.com cancelled effective Sept 30 with a Zillow listing deep-dive underway.

wins.description: The cleanest operating week in the portfolio - 93% occupancy, 95.91% pre-leased, a 50% close rate on tours, and delinquency down to a single pending payment. The team is raising application and admin fees from a position of strength rather than discounting into it.

Occupancy up to 97.5% from 96.6% and the highest in the portfolio, with five tours completed and three more booked. Fee waivers were deployed as a closing tool while the $1,450 rate held - volume without rate erosion.

Marketing is outrunning operations: leases rose from 21 to 45 with cost per lease down more than $100 after the PMAX upgrade, and the property led the portfolio in new Google reviews. Pending applications were cleaned from 79 to 34, which is what makes the occupancy projections credible.
Leases quadrupled and cost per lease nearly halved following a website refresh and increased PMAX spend - the highest-ROI marketing change made anywhere in the portfolio this month.

Occupancy at 90.74% trending to 95.3%, turnover at just 4.63%, delinquency exceptionally low, and an 8-of-9 application rate at a 75% close. The signature upgrade package also came down to $1,950 per unit from $2,500, saving $550 on every unit touched.

17 applications and seven approvals in a single week with 11 rent-ready units to absorb them, fully staffed, and the best cost per conversion in the Central/West group at $31.22 - which is why it is getting the reallocated Apartments.com budget.

Portfolio-wide PPC conversions rose over 7% to more than 600 at roughly $32 per conversion, and the portfolio gained 67 new Google reviews. Apartments.com packages are being cut at underperforming properties and the savings redeployed to PPC and PMAX where cost per conversion justifies it.

The 2027 budget process now runs on locked templates and standardized SOPs with a 5% or $5,000 variance-comment threshold. Maria's Tampa submission came in detailed enough to be adopted as the house standard for every other region.

recommendations.title: Fix the Skye Reserve org chart before underwriting the recap
recommendations.detail: The MF1/Berkshire term sheet lands this week against an operating record of 78% occupancy and 31 down units. Every week the regional manager seat and Tina's backfill stay open, the counterparty's stabilized-value argument gets weaker and the interest-reserve gap ($4M versus $850K) gets harder to close in our favor. Close the regional hire and name a single accountable owner for down-unit remediation before the term sheet is countered.

recommendations.title: Treat the Newmark repair packet as a hard Sept 30 deliverable, not a documentation exercise
recommendations.detail: Three assets are blocked on the same packet and the original July 30 requirement is already missed. The binding question is not whether the work was done - it is whether ZMR can prove it. Get explicit written lender guidance on the asphalt scope at Skye Oaks before committing budget, and set a Friday internal cutoff so Megan has a full week of float before the deadline.

recommendations.title: Stop making decisions off the Chimney Hill and Upland delinquency reports until they reconcile
recommendations.detail: Chimney Hill shows discrepancies up to $30,000 from misincluded past-due notices, and Upland's effective occupancy of ~72% only became visible once concession burn-off was separated from true delinquency. Standardize one delinquency report format across both, with move-in date, 12-month late count, concession end date and eviction-risk score, then re-baseline.

recommendations.title: Push the screening changes portfolio-wide rather than asset-by-asset
recommendations.detail: Upland ended second-chance approvals and began denying prior evictions and bankruptcies; Chimney Hill is building a payment-pattern column; Skye Ridge is fighting 9% November retention. These are the same problem. Florida income-to-rent thresholds as low as 2.0x and credit screening below 560 were flagged separately in the AM team call - set one portfolio standard and measure bad debt against it.

recommendations.title: Redeploy marketing spend on the evidence already in hand
recommendations.detail: The Sky Oaks website refresh plus PMAX increase quadrupled leases and halved cost per lease. Parks at Walnut converts at $31.22. The Flats produces zero Zillow leases. Chimney Hill's lead-to-prospect conversion fell 30% on $46 conversions. The data supports a faster reallocation than the current property-by-property approval cycle allows.

recommendations.title: Make the capital draw workflow deterministic
recommendations.detail: Title search plus a $175 wire is now required on every Preserve draw, lenders are referencing outdated capital budgets, and $130K-$173K reallocations are being rediscovered each cycle. Publish one draw SOP covering reallocation file, proof of payment, aging AP detail and title search, and separate capital from replacement draws in the file structure.

recommendations.title: Resolve the rent write-off GL coding before the 2027 budget locks
recommendations.detail: $90,754 in write-offs through September 2026 are inconsistently coded, with ~$31,000 reducing income accounts instead of hitting expense. Budgets map to 5800-01 while ARA Yardi defaults to 6800-01. Net bad debt is correct but market rent reporting is at risk of misstatement. Decide the code now so the 2027 budget and September close are built on it.
